1.0.title: Constitutional Control and Election Authority
1.0.text: The MPU Constitution controls in the event of any conflict. The Electoral Committee sets and publishes election guidelines under Article V, Section 3(d), consistent with Article V, Section 10, and all other controlling provisions. These rules regulate election administration; they do not amend the Constitution or create new constitutional qualifications. A genuine matter not covered by the Constitution shall be handled through Article XII.

1.1.title: Constitutional Authority, Publication, and Lacuna
1.1.text:
Electoral Committee election procedures. Article V, Section 3(d) authorizes the Electoral Committee to set and publish election guidelines and requires those guidelines to conform to Article V, Section 10. For the 2026 election, the Committee shall complete review and final adoption of these Rules by Sunday, October 4, 2026; transmit the adopted Rules to the MPU Executive Council on Monday, October 5, 2026, for administrative notice and coordination; and officially publish the Rules to the membership on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, through designated MPU communication channels. The Executive Council receipt is an administrative notice and does not become an additional approval requirement unless the Constitution requires it.

Committee publication backstop. For orderly election administration, the Electoral Committee has established Sunday, October 25, 2026, as the latest internal publication backstop for any supplemental election procedure intended to govern the November 15, 2026, election. This twenty-one-day backstop is a 2026 committee safeguard and is not stated in Article XII as an independent constitutional publication requirement.

Genuine constitutional gaps. Article XII governs matters or issues not covered or provided for in the Constitution. Under Article XII, the Executive Council presents such a matter to the General Assembly for deliberation and decision. If the matter is urgent or an emergency that cannot await the General Assembly, the President, in consultation with at least two (2) other Executive Council members, may take appropriate action and thereafter report to the General Assembly. The Electoral Committee shall not use an administrative guideline to amend the Constitution or independently resolve a genuine constitutional lacuna reserved to Article XII.

1.2.title: Use of Technology—Official Notices, Election Information, Consent, Acceptance, Payments, and Records
1.2.text:
To the extent permitted by the MPU Constitution and applicable law, approved electronic methods may be used for election administration, official notices, candidate communications, voter and candidate education, publication of election information, payments, and recordkeeping. Use of technology under this section does not authorize electronic voting.

(a) Official Electronic Channels and Notices. The Electoral Committee may designate official election communication channels, including email, text message, the official MPU WhatsApp platform, and the MPU portal. Official notices may include nomination information, acceptance deadlines, withdrawal notices, corrections under Section 3.4, screening or presence-verification communications, election schedules, and other election-administration notices. Member- or candidate-specific notices requiring an individual response should be directed to the verified contact information on record or another verified channel designated by that person.

(b) WhatsApp Publication, Financial Standing, and Election Education. The official MPU WhatsApp platform may be used to publish general voter and candidate education, the election timetable, deadlines and reminders, financial-standing information used for election administration, provisional and final voter or candidate information, sample-ballot education, Election Day instructions, corrections, and certified results. Where financial standing is published, the posting should be limited to the election-relevant standing customarily used by MPU and should not disclose bank-account information, payment credentials, or other unnecessary private financial details. Official voter-education communications shall be neutral and shall not promote or criticize any candidate.

(c) Status and Authentication of Published Lists. Any voter, financial-standing, or candidate list published for election administration shall be clearly identified as PROVISIONAL or FINAL and shall include the publication date and, where material, the time. An official Electoral Committee posting should be identifiable as an MPU 2026 Electoral Committee communication. A forwarded screenshot, member repost, comment, reaction, poll response, or other unofficial reproduction does not replace the controlling official record. The Final Voter Register and Final Candidate List published on November 4, 2026, shall serve as the controlling election-administration records, subject only to documented administrative correction, a properly recorded late withdrawal, or action required under the MPU Constitution or these Rules.

(d) Signatures, Consent, Acceptance, Switches, and Withdrawals. A signature, consent, acceptance, switch request, or withdrawal required under these rules may be satisfied by an electronic signature or a clear written confirmation transmitted from the member's or candidate's verified email address, verified WhatsApp number, Candidate Portal account, or another approved attributable electronic method. The communication must clearly identify the action being taken and be retrievable and printable. A reaction emoji, "like," informal group comment, forwarded message, or ambiguous response shall not by itself constitute formal acceptance, withdrawal, switch, complaint, or other required filing.

(e) Payments. An electronic payment method, including Zelle or bank transfer, may be used for dues or other payments relevant to Good Standing verification, provided a receipt or other verifiable record is retained. Electronic payment is a method of payment only. It does not extend or alter the constitutional time at which financial standing must be satisfied. The October 18 eligibility-record cutoff is an administrative records freeze under Section 2.0, not a new opportunity to cure or redefine a constitutional eligibility requirement.

(f) Electronic Delivery, Timestamp, Failed Delivery, Corrections, and Records. Unless a published rule states otherwise, electronic election deadlines are measured in Eastern Time (ET). An official electronic communication is timestamped when transmitted through the designated channel to the verified address, number, account, or official group. If the Electoral Committee receives a bounce-back, failed-delivery notice, or other reliable indication that an individual notice did not reach the intended verified contact, the Committee should make a reasonable attempt through another approved channel and document that attempt. A corrected official posting of the 2026 election shall be clearly marked CORRECTION or SUPERSEDING NOTICE, dated and timed, and both the original and corrected communication shall be retained in the election record. Official electronic election communications and attachments shall be retained in a retrievable and printable form, including sufficient information to identify the sender, recipient or channel, and date/time of transmission. Candidate- or member-specific private information should be communicated privately unless publication is required by the MPU Constitution or a duly adopted MPU rule.

(g) Secret Paper Ballot. Technology under this section is for administration and records only. Official voting remains by secret paper ballot under Article V, Sections 3(e) and 10, using Sections 4.0–6.1. Voting by email, WhatsApp, text message, portal, or electronic ballot is not authorized.

1.3.title: Consolidated Election Timetable
1.3.text:
Date or deadline | Existing V20 milestone
October 4 / 5 / 6 | Planned EC adoption / Executive Council administrative notice / member publication
October 18 | Official eligibility records cutoff; administrative freeze only
October 19–25 | Nomination & Candidate Acceptance Period. Nominations may be submitted during this period. Every nominee must personally provide affirmative acceptance through an approved EC method. Only constitutionally eligible active members may nominate or be nominated.
October 25, 11:59 PM ET | Nomination and affirmative acceptance deadline: one written office switch must be timely.
October 25 | EC internal publication backstop for supplemental procedures
October 26–28 | Candidate screening
October 31 | Provisional Candidate List
November 3 | Correction, clarification, and complaint window ends
November 3, 11:59 PM ET | Regular withdrawal deadline
November 4 | Final Candidate List and Final Voter Register
November 15 | General Election Meeting: logistics announced through Appendix L

The nomination and candidate acceptance period is October 19–25, 2026. Election Day venue and times remain in the separate official notice. Portal testing dates are not incorporated into these rules.

2.0.title: Eligibility Records Cutoff - Administrative Freeze Only
2.0.text: The October 18, 2026, Official Eligibility Records Cutoff is an election-administration records-freeze date. It identifies the official membership, attendance, financial, LGA, and related records the Electoral Committee will use for screening and voter-register administration. It does not extend, replace, or create a constitutional deadline for satisfying financial standing, attendance, membership duration, or any other eligibility requirement. Constitutional eligibility remains governed by the MPU Constitution, including the applicable requirement that dues and other qualifying conditions be satisfied when the Constitution requires them.

2.1.title: Self-Nomination—2026 Electoral Committee Administrative Procedure
2.1.text: Article V, Section 10 permits eligible active members to nominate candidates and to be nominated, but it does not expressly address self-nomination or require a seconder. For the 2026 election, the Electoral Committee will accept self-nomination as a uniform administrative procedure, provided the member independently satisfies all constitutional eligibility requirements. This procedure does not create a new constitutional qualification or alter any constitutional eligibility standard.

2.2.title: Multiple-Office Nominations—2026 Ballot Administration Procedure
2.2.text:
(a) For 2026 ballot administration, no candidate shall appear on the final ballot for more than one elected office in the same election. Article V, Section 4 expressly prohibits an officer from holding more than one position at a time; it does not separately prescribe how multiple simultaneous candidacies must be administered. The one-candidate/one-office ballot rule is therefore a uniform Electoral Committee procedure designed to prevent a simultaneous-office conflict and to produce an administrable final ballot. It does not add a constitutional eligibility requirement.

(b) Where a member receives multiple nominations, the earliest valid nomination received and timestamped will remain the operative nomination unless the member submits a written change before the published deadline. Subsequent nominations will not be placed on the ballot unless the member timely elects to switch. The system shall automatically reject the later nomination from ballot consideration and record the date and time of the rejection. The automated rule is applied uniformly without discretionary selection by the Electoral Committee.

(c) Affirmative acceptance required—no consent, no ballot. No name shall be placed on the final ballot unless the member has submitted written acceptance for that specific operative office by the acceptance deadline. A nomination without acceptance is treated as an automatic declination. This avoids electing a person who is not interested in serving.

(d) If a member fails to elect one office by the deadline, the first nomination remains operative but still requires acceptance under 2.2(c). If the member accepted the first nomination, the first stands and subsequent nominations are automatically deemed declined, rejected, and recorded. If the member accepted none, all nominations are deemed declined, and the member shall not appear on the ballot for any office. This reflects lack of consent, not punishment.

(e) A member may file ONE written switch before the deadline to replace the operative nomination with a later nomination. Upon receipt, the system automatically replaces and records the change. One switch only. After the deadline, the operative nomination is final.

2.3.title: Acceptance Deadline
2.3.text: For the 2026 election, all nominations and nominee acceptances must be completed no later than 11:59 PM Eastern Time (ET) on Sunday, October 25, 2026, in accordance with the published 2026 Election Timetable. Acceptance must be affirmative and in writing or through an approved electronic method under Section 1.2. A nomination that has not been personally accepted by the nominee by this deadline will not proceed to candidate screening or final ballot consideration. Silence or failure to submit acceptance by the deadline means no acceptance and therefore no ballot placement under Sections 2.2(c) and 2.2(d).

2.4.title: Candidate Acceptance & Profile Form
2.4.text:
Each candidate whose operative nomination remains active shall submit an official MPU Candidate Acceptance & Profile Form by the published acceptance deadline. The form shall document, at minimum, the candidate's full name and LGA; the office sought; affirmative acceptance of that specific nomination; confirmation of willingness to serve if elected; acknowledgment of the candidate-presence requirement under 4.1; confirmation that the candidate meets the applicable constitutional qualifications for the office; current contact information; and a short candidate profile or biography for member information.

Submission of the profile form does not create any qualification beyond those required by the MPU Constitution and these published election procedures. Eligibility shall be determined from the Constitution and certified MPU records. The form is an administrative record used to document acceptance, candidate information, and compliance with the published deadline.

The form shall be submitted through the MPU Candidate Portal or another submission method expressly published by the Electoral Committee under Section 1.2. Electronic submissions, including email or WhatsApp where authorized, must be attributable to the candidate through verified contact information, capable of being retained and printed, and received by the published deadline. If affirmative acceptance is not received by 11:59 PM Eastern Time (ET) on Sunday, October 25, 2026, the nomination shall be treated as not accepted under Section 2.2(c).

3.0.title: Candidate Screening—Article V, Section 4 Office-Holding Restrictions
3.0.text: During candidate screening, the Electoral Committee shall verify the applicable office-holding restrictions in Article V, Section 4, including prior service and term limits, the one-position-at-a-time rule, and the spouse office-holding restriction. Article V, Section 4, provides that no husband and wife shall hold office at the same time. Because the Constitution prohibits simultaneous office-holding but does not expressly state that spouses may not both be candidates, the Committee shall not create an automatic candidacy disqualification solely because both spouses are nominated. Any potential simultaneous-office conflict shall be flagged and documented before final certification. If the Constitution does not supply the method for resolving an actual unresolved conflict, the matter shall be handled under Article XII. This screening check shall be applied uniformly and shall not create any qualification or disqualification beyond the Constitution.

3.1.title: Provisional Candidate List
3.1.text: After the October 25 nomination and acceptance deadline and candidate screening on October 26–28, the Electoral Committee shall publish the PROVISIONAL Candidate List on Saturday, October 31, 2026. The list remains subject to correction, clarification, and complaint through November 3 under Section 3.2.

3.2.title: Corrections, Clarifications, and Complaints
3.2.text: Through November 3, submit documented clerical errors, omissions, office-placement discrepancies, or screening-record questions to the Electoral Committee using its designated official channel under Section 1.2. Identify the affected record and supporting evidence. The Committee shall retain the submission and record its administrative disposition and governing basis. This process does not waive deadlines or constitutional eligibility. A matter outside election administration must follow the applicable constitutional route; a written petition falling under Article V, Section 8 remains subject to that Board process, and a genuine constitutional gap remains subject to Article XII. This section creates no new appeal authority or disciplinary power.

3.3.title: Candidate Withdrawal: Regular or Late
3.3.text:
A candidate withdrawal must be submitted in writing to the Electoral Committee through an approved attributable method under Section 1.2. The regular withdrawal deadline is 11:59 PM ET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Retain the candidate’s request and receipt timestamp. Apply the following controls according to when withdrawal occurs:

Before ballot printing, the candidate's name shall be removed from the ballot.

After printing but before voting begins: the candidate's name may remain printed, but a notice shall be posted stating that votes cast for the withdrawn candidate will not be counted.

After voting has begun, the ballot shall not be altered. If the withdrawn candidate receives the result that otherwise would have elected the candidate, the office shall be declared vacant and handled under Section 7.7 and the applicable constitutional provisions, including the presidential exception to Article V, Section 5.

3.4.title: Correction of Omission or Misspelling
3.4.text: If a candidate name is omitted or misspelled after printing, post a written correction at the gate and voting table before voting. (ii) announce the correction three times verbally; (iii) record the correction in the minutes and Result Form; and (iv) if the error is misleading, reprint that office section as a clearly marked handwritten correction slip stapled to the regular ballot, consistent with 7.6(c).

3.5.title: Final Candidate List and Sample Ballot
3.5.text:
After the regular withdrawal deadline of 11:59 PM ET on Tuesday, November 3, the Electoral Committee shall publish the FINAL Candidate List on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Within each contested office, names shall be listed alphabetically by surname unless the Constitution expressly requires another order. The Final Voter Register is also published November 4 under Section 1.2(c).

After the Final Candidate List is established, the Electoral Committee shall prepare and distribute a sample ballot showing the qualified candidates and the office for which each candidate is standing, including the applicable LGA-specific Board seats. Every sample ballot distributed electronically or in print shall be prominently marked "SAMPLE BALLOT—FOR EDUCATION ONLY—NOT FOR VOTING."

3.6.title: Distribution of Candidate Information and Sample Ballot
3.6.text:
The Electoral Committee shall distribute the Provisional Candidate List, Final Candidate List, sample ballot, and other official candidate information through designated MPU communication channels. The official MPU WhatsApp platform may be used for publication together with email, the MPU portal, or another channel identified by the Electoral Committee. Each published list shall be clearly labeled PROVISIONAL or FINAL and shall display its publication date and, where material, the publication time.

Members and candidates should promptly report clerical errors, name misspellings, office-placement errors, omissions, or other documented record discrepancies within the applicable timetable window. Corrections discovered after ballot printing remain governed by Section 3.4. Publication of candidate information or a sample ballot through WhatsApp, email, or the MPU portal does not authorize electronic voting; official voting remains by secret paper ballot under Section 1.2(g).

4.0.title: Election Day Event - MPU 2026 General Election Meeting

4.1.title: Candidate Presence at the Call for Election
4.1.text:
Per Art. V Sec. 10, any member seeking any office must be present at the meeting for the election. The Electoral Committee shall verify candidate presence before voting begins. Verification shall be applied uniformly without discretionary selection.

If an operative candidate who affirmatively accepted under 2.2(c) is not present at the call for election, the candidate's name shall remain printed on the ballot, but votes cast for that candidate shall not be counted for that office. The remaining sixteen office sections on the ballot shall remain valid.

If the absent candidate is the sole candidate for that office, the office shall be declared vacant and handled under Section 7.7, including the presidential exception to Article V, Section 5.

Before the ballot box is opened, the Electoral Committee shall prepare and record the official Present Candidates List and compare it with the final ballot.

4.2.title: Ballot Box Opening Verification
4.2.text: Before the first ballot is issued, the Electoral Committee shall visibly confirm that the official ballot box is empty and shall then secure the box for voting. The Election Day record shall document the date and time of verification; the ballot-box identifier, if one is used; any seal or control number used; the names of Electoral Committee officials present; the names of any authorized observers present; any objection raised before the box is secured; and the initials or signatures of the presiding Electoral Committee official and at least one additional Electoral Committee member. If no objection is raised, the record may state "No objection recorded." This verification supplements the ballot-box preparation requirement already stated in Section 4.0.

5.0.title: Gate Accreditation and Ticket Issuance
5.0.text:
At the gate, the election official shall verify the member against the approved voter eligibility/Good Standing records and confirm the member's LGA. A numbered raffle ticket in the applicable color—BLUE for Ahiazu Mbaise, GREEN for Ezinihitte Mbaise, or YELLOW for Aboh Mbaise—shall then be issued. The clerk shall record the ticket number next to the member's name and mark Present at Gate. The ticket is an accreditation and ballot-control document only; it is not a ballot and does not by itself establish that the member has voted.

After gate accreditation, the member shall proceed to the voting table. Ticket surrender, voter-register signature, ballot issuance, and present at voting verification are governed by Section 5.4.

5.1.title: Ballot Structure
5.1.text: The ballot contains 17 office sections: 10 executive offices—President, Vice President, Secretary, Assistant Secretary, Financial Secretary, Treasurer, PRO, Director of Social, Provost 1, and Provost 2—plus 7 Board positions: Board Chairman (all eligible voters), 2 Ahiazu Mbaise seats, 2 Ezinihitte Mbaise seats, and 2 Aboh Mbaise seats. Ballot colors are BLUE for Ahiazu Mbaise, GREEN for Ezinihitte Mbaise, and YELLOW for Aboh Mbaise. Other LGA sections are greyed and marked DO NOT MARK. For election administration, the three LGA classifications are Aboh Mbaise, Ahiazu Mbaise, and Ezinihitte Mbaise. Ahiara is part of Ahiazu Mbaise and is not a separate LGA classification.

5.2.title: LGA Isolation
5.2.text: Per Art. V Sec. 10, LGA Board positions are voted on only by members of that LGA. No proxy voting. Marking another LGA section voids that office section only under 5.3; the remainder of the ballot remains valid.

5.3.title: Shading, Voids, and Replacement Ballots
5.3.text:
VALID: One X or one check mark clearly placed in the appropriate candidate box shall be counted.

ABSTENTION: A blank office section is an abstention. It counts as no vote for that office; the other properly marked office sections remain valid.

VOID - OFFICE ONLY: If a voter marks more candidates than permitted for an office, that office selection is void. All other properly marked office sections on the ballot remain valid.

LGA VIOLATION - OFFICE ONLY: An LGA voting violation shall void only the affected LGA office selection. For example, a BLUE/Ahiazu Mbaise voter marking a GREEN/Ezinihitte Mbaise Board position shall not have that GREEN selection counted. The remaining valid selections on the ballot remain unaffected.

REPLACEMENT BEFORE DEPOSIT: A voter who discovers an error before depositing the ballot may request a replacement without disclosing how the ballot was marked. The spoiled ballot shall be surrendered, marked CANCELLED without examination of voter choices, retained separately for reconciliation, and replaced.

VOID - WHOLE BALLOT: A ballot containing the voter's name, signature, telephone number, membership number, or other information reasonably capable of identifying the voter shall be void in its entirety because ballot secrecy has been compromised. An accidental stray mark that does not identify the voter shall not by itself void the entire ballot.

Candidate-presence exclusions are governed by Section 4.1. They affect the relevant office only; other properly marked office selections remain valid.

5.4.title: Voting Table, Ballot Issuance, and Secret Voting
5.4.text:
Election Day voting flow: Gate Accreditation -> Ticket Issued -> Voting Table -> Ticket Surrendered -> Voter Register Signed -> Ballot Issued -> Secret Vote -> Ballot Deposited -> Reconciliation -> Counting.

At the voting table, the member shall surrender the numbered accreditation ticket and sign the voter register before receiving a ballot. The election official shall confirm the ticket color/LGA against the register, issue the corresponding BLUE, GREEN, or YELLOW ballot, and record Present at Voting. A ballot shall not be issued without the required ticket surrender and voter-register signature, except where a documented administrative correction is authorized under these published rules.

After receiving the ballot, the voter shall proceed to the designated secret-voting area, mark the ballot privately in accordance with Sections 5.1–5.3, and personally deposit the ballot in the official ballot box. No person may inspect or require disclosure of how a voter marked the ballot.

Voting shall be by secret paper ballot only; no proxy voting shall be permitted

Each eligible voter may cast one vote for each applicable office

All eligible members may vote for the 10 Executive Council offices and the Board Chairman

Only eligible members of each respective LGA may vote for that LGA's two Board representative seats; and

Ballots shall be marked, reviewed for voter-detected errors before deposit, and handled under Sections 5.1 through 5.3.

5.5.title: Assisted Voting
5.5.text: An eligible voter who, because of a disability or other legitimate limitation, is unable to mark or deposit the ballot independently may request assistance from the Electoral Committee before marking the ballot. The voter may be assisted by one trusted adult chosen by the voter, provided the helper is not a candidate for an office appearing on that voter's ballot. If the voter does not wish to choose a helper, two neutral Electoral Committee members may provide assistance. Assistance shall be limited to carrying out the voter's expressed choices. No helper or Electoral Committee member may influence, suggest, disclose, or require disclosure of the voter's selections. The Election Day Incident/Assistance/Challenge Log shall record that assistance was requested and provided, the name(s) of the helper(s), and the time of assistance, but shall not record how the voter voted. Assisted voting does not constitute proxy voting because the eligible voter personally directs and casts the voter's own ballot.

6.0.title: Close of Voting

6.1.title: Reconciliation
6.1.text:
Before counting begins, the Electoral Committee shall reconcile the voting records.

Voter control: Tickets surrendered for voting = voter-register signatures = initial ballots issued. Replacement ballots do not create additional voter-register signatures, surrendered tickets, or voting entitlements.

Physical ballot control: Total physical ballots issued = initial ballots issued + replacement ballots issued. Total physical ballots issued = ballots deposited + spoiled/cancelled ballots retained + any issued but undeposited ballots separately documented. Opening stock = total physical ballots issued + unused stock. Record replacements and surrendered cancelled ballots separately; a cancelled ballot is never counted as a deposited vote.

Record and explain every discrepancy before certification. Record tickets issued but not surrendered separately; they are not ballots cast. Retain stock, issuance, replacement, cancellation, deposit, and unused-ballot totals by ballot color as needed for reconciliation.

Reconciliation shall be completed separately as necessary to confirm LGA ballot distribution and compliance with Section 7.0.

Candidate presence shall have been verified and recorded before voting pursuant to Section 4.1.

Records supporting reconciliation, candidate presence, acceptance, nominations, notices, corrections, withdrawals, payments, and election certification may be maintained electronically in accordance with Section 1.2, provided the records are retrievable, printable, and retained in the official election file. Technology shall not replace the secret paper ballot required for voting.

7.0.title: Counting—LGA Isolation—Article V, Section 10
7.0.text:
After the ballot box is closed and reconciliation is completed, ballots shall be separated into three LGA groups: BLUE—Ahiazu Mbaise; GREEN—Ezinihitte Mbaise; and YELLOW—Aboh Mbaise.

The 10 Executive Council positions and the Board Chairman position shall be counted using all three ballot groups because every eligible member is entitled to vote for those offices.

The two Ahiazu Mbaise Board positions shall be counted from BLUE ballots only. The two Ezinihitte Mbaise Board positions shall be counted from GREEN ballots only. The two Aboh Mbaise Board positions shall be counted from YELLOW ballots only.

This implements Article V, Section 10, under which the LGA representatives on the Board are voted for only by members of the respective LGA.

Votes shall be tallied separately for each office using an official tally sheet. A visible tally method such as IIII may be used during the count, but the final totals shall be entered on and certified through the Official Result Form.

7.1.title: Counting Team—Caller + Two Independent Recorders
7.1.text:
The counting team shall consist of at least three designated election officials with clearly separated duties.

Person 1—Caller/Ballot Controller: Opens the ballot box under the supervision of the Electoral Committee Chair, separates ballots into the required BLUE, GREEN, and YELLOW groups, and calls each valid vote aloud by office and candidate. The Caller shall not record vote totals. Each ballot shall be displayed sufficiently for the two recorders and authorized observers to verify the announced vote while preserving ballot secrecy.

Person 2 - Recorder A / Wall Tally: Independently records each announced vote on the visible wall or chart tally using the agreed tally method, such as IIII. Recorder A shall not handle ballots.

Person 3 - Recorder B / Official Result Form: Independently records the same announced votes on the Official Result Form. Recorder B shall not handle ballots.

7.2.title: Counting Oversight and Authorized Observers
7.2.text:
Ballot counting and reconciliation shall be conducted under Sections 7.0, 7.1, 7.3, and 6.1 in the presence of the Chair/Chief Electoral Officer and designated tellers. The Electoral Committee may also permit authorized observers in accordance with the published election procedures. Observers may witness the count but shall not handle ballots, direct tellers, interfere with counting, or compromise ballot secrecy.

The same observation rules shall be applied uniformly. Candidates are not automatically entitled to serve as tellers or handle ballots merely because they are candidates; any observer access must be authorized and administered consistently by the Electoral Committee.

Candidate Observer Protocol. For each contested office, each candidate may designate no more than one observer for the counting process, subject to available space and the same uniform rules for all candidates. An observer may witness the count from the designated observer area and may see and hear the announced vote totals but shall not handle ballots, touch tally or result forms, direct tellers, interrupt the count, or compromise ballot secrecy. Any concern raised by an observer shall be directed to the Electoral Committee Chair or presiding election official and, where material, recorded in the Election Day Incident / Assistance / Challenge Log. Observer participation does not make the observer an election official and does not give the observer authority to certify the result.

7.3.title: Tally Comparison, Recount, Corrections, and Certification
7.3.text:
At the completion of each office, the Wall Tally and Official Result Form shall be compared. If the totals do not agree, counting for that office shall be paused, and the ballots for that office shall be recounted before proceeding.

No erasures shall be made on official tally records. Any correction shall be made by striking through the incorrect entry with a single line, entering the corrected figure, and having both recorders initial the correction.

Ballot and voter reconciliation shall be conducted under Section 6.1 by the counting team and Electoral Committee together. No single recorder shall unilaterally certify reconciliation.

After all offices have been counted and reconciled, the caller, both recorders/tellers, and electoral committee chair shall review the final totals before certification. Authorized observers may witness the process but shall not handle ballots or direct the count.

Documented Recount Request. Before certification of an office result, the Electoral Committee may order one recount where there is an objective, documented reason to question the count, including an arithmetic discrepancy, disagreement between official tally records, an unresolved ballot-classification issue, or another specific counting irregularity capable of affecting the result. A request based only on dissatisfaction with the outcome, without a stated objective basis, does not by itself require a recount. Any recount ordered shall be conducted under the same counting controls in Sections 7.0, 7.1, and 7.3 and recorded in the election file.

7.4.title: Simple Majority
7.4.text:
Per Art. V Sec. 3, candidates are elected by a simple majority of the votes of eligible members present and voting. For these procedures, a simple majority means more than fifty percent (>50%) of the valid votes cast for that specific office.

A valid vote is one properly marked X or check mark for a candidate or a valid YES/NO selection in an uncontested race.

A blank selection is an abstention. It does not count as a valid vote for that office, but it does not affect the validity of properly marked selections for the other offices on the ballot.

The following are also excluded when calculating valid votes for that office: an overvote or other office-specific void under Section 5.3; an LGA voting violation affecting that office; and a ballot voided in its entirety under Section 5.3.

For each office, classify ballots without overlap: Valid Votes = Ballots Cast applicable to that office − Whole-Ballot Voids − Blanks/Abstentions on remaining ballots − Office-Specific Exclusions on remaining ballots. Office-specific exclusions include overvotes, ineligible LGA selections, and votes for candidates absent at the call for election. Do not subtract an exclusion twice. For LGA seats, use only ballots of the eligible LGA as the starting count.

The successful candidate must receive more than half of the valid votes cast for that office.

Example: 32 valid votes require 17 votes for a simple majority. A 16-16 result does not constitute a simple majority and proceeds under Section 7.6.

For an uncontested YES/NO race, YES must exceed NO and must also exceed 50% of the valid YES/NO votes cast; otherwise the office is vacant under Section 7.7.

7.5.title: Uncontested Race—No Acclamation
7.5.text: Even where only one eligible candidate appears for an office, the candidate shall appear on the secret ballot as YES [ ] / NO [ ]. Acclamation is not used because Art. V Sec. 10 requires a secret ballot.

7.6.title: Tie and Failure to Obtain Simple Majority
7.6.text:
(a) Tie for Highest Vote. If two or more candidates are tied for the highest number of valid votes and no candidate has obtained a simple majority, an immediate runoff shall be conducted among the tied candidates.

(b) No Majority / No Tie. If no candidate receives more than 50% of the valid votes cast and there is no tie, the two candidates receiving the highest numbers of valid votes shall proceed to an immediate runoff. Example: A = 18 votes (45%), B = 14 votes (35%), C = 8 votes (20%); valid votes = 40 and majority required = 21. No candidate has 21 votes, so A and B proceed to runoff.

If second place is tied—for example, A = 18, B = 11, and C = 11—the runoff shall initially include A, B, and C. If that three-candidate runoff still produces no simple majority, the two candidates with the highest vote totals in that runoff shall proceed to a second and final runoff.

(c) Runoff Ballot. A runoff may use either a fresh official ballot using the regular ballot format, with only the runoff office counted, or a clearly marked handwritten runoff ballot listing only the runoff office and eligible runoff candidates. Either method must preserve the secret-ballot requirement.

(d) Eligible Runoff Voters. Only eligible members who are entitled to vote in the election and who remain present for the runoff may participate.

(e) Majority Required. A runoff winner must receive more than 50% of the valid votes cast in that runoff.

(f) Final Runoff Tie. If the final runoff results in a tie, the office shall be declared vacant and handled under Section 7.7 and the applicable constitutional provisions, including the presidential exception to Article V, Section 5. No coin toss, drawing of lots, or other random selection shall be used.

EC REVIEW ITEM BEFORE ADOPTION: Section 7.6(b) does not specify which two candidates advance if second place remains tied after the three-candidate runoff (for example, 18–11–11 again). No additional tie-breaker is adopted in this draft. The EC must review this procedural omission under its constitutional mandate and refer it if it cannot be resolved administratively.

7.7.title: Vacancy
7.7.text: If an office is not filled because an uncontested candidate fails to obtain the required simple majority, no candidate shall be declared elected for that office. Any resulting vacancy shall be handled strictly under the applicable MPU constitutional provisions. For an office other than the President, Article V, Section 5 provides that the President shall appoint an active member temporarily until an election is held to fill the vacancy at the next general meeting, or, if not feasible at that meeting, no later than three (3) months; that vacancy election is conducted by the Executive Council in accordance with Article V, Section 10. Article V, Section 5 expressly excludes the office of president. Any unresolved presidential-vacancy question or other genuine constitutional gap shall be handled under the applicable constitutional provisions, including Article XII where necessary. These rules create no additional disqualification from the temporary appointment.

8.0.title: Election Records, Certification, and Publication of Results
8.0.text:
The Electoral Committee shall preserve the official election record, including the Committee appointment and General Assembly approval/ratification record required by the Constitution; nomination records; Candidate Acceptance & Profile Forms; acceptance and switch records; eligibility determinations; Provisional and Final Candidate Lists and sample ballots; presence-verification records; voter-register and ticket reconciliation records; spoiled/cancelled-ballot logs; tally sheets; recount requests and recount records; Election Day Incident / Assistance / Challenge Logs; ballot-box opening/seal records; constitutional-issue referral records; the Election Day Notice; runoff records; correction notices; withdrawal notices; and the final certified result form.

Records may be retained in paper or retrievable electronic form. Electronic records shall be stored in a format that can be retrieved and printed and shall be transferred to or retained by the appropriate MPU record custodian, including the Secretary, where required by the Constitution.

Certified election results shall be announced at the election meeting and may thereafter be published through the designated official MPU communication channels, including the official MPU WhatsApp platform, email, or the MPU portal. The published result notice shall be clearly identifiable as an Electoral Committee communication and retained in the official election record. Publication of certified results shall not disclose how any individual member voted and shall preserve ballot secrecy.

9.0.title: Election Day Conduct Integrity and Incident Response
9.0.text: This section addresses conduct, ballot secrecy, election interference, protective administrative action, documentation, and referral. Operational voting and counting procedures appear in Sections 4.0–8.0. The MPU Constitution controls at all times.

9.1.title: Member Conduct During the Election Meeting

9.2.title: Protection of Secret Ballot and Voting Integrity
9.2.text:
Article V, Sections 3(e) and 10, require election by secret ballot, prohibit proxy voting, and limit each eligible member to one vote for each applicable office. To preserve those constitutional requirements:

No person may intentionally interfere with another member's secret vote or require disclosure of how another member voted

No person may vote on behalf of another member, vote more than once, or attempt to place an unauthorized ballot into the ballot box

Photographing, video-recording, or deliberately displaying a completed ballot in a manner that compromises ballot secrecy is prohibited;

No unauthorized person may possess, handle, alter, remove, or interfere with official ballots, the ballot box, voter register, tally sheets, result forms, reconciliation records, or other controlled election materials; and

No person may deliberately interfere with counting, reconciliation, certification, or another member's lawful exercise of the right to vote.

Ballot validity remains governed by Sections 5.1 through 5.3. Misconduct is not, by itself, a basis to void an otherwise valid ballot unless the published ballot-validity rules require that result.

9.3.title: Electioneering in the Controlled Voting and Counting Area
9.3.text: Under the Electoral Committee's authority in Article V, Section 3(d) to conduct the election and publish guidelines consistent with Article V, Section 10, campaigning, solicitation of votes, distribution or display of campaign materials, or other candidate advocacy shall not occur inside the designated voting or counting area once voting begins. This restriction does not prohibit ordinary member conversation outside the controlled election area, provided it does not disrupt the meeting or interfere with voting, counting, or ballot secrecy.
